exhibits.title: Orders, 1520
exhibits.body: To OR as soon as available. Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV given at 1515.

questions.stem: The surgeon arrives at 1540 to obtain consent. The client received hydromorphone at 1515. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tell the surgeon the opioid time and how alert the client is
Witness the signature if the client can restate the risks
Document the time and the client's understanding
Explain the risks of the surgery yourself before the surgeon arrives
Withhold all further analgesia until the consent form is signed

rationale.correct: Consent is the surgeon's duty; the nurse reports medication and alertness, witnesses and documents.

perOption.a: The surgeon judges capacity; the nurse provides the information.
perOption.b: A small opioid dose does not remove capacity if the client understands.
perOption.d: Explaining the procedure is the surgeon's role.
perOption.e: Pain control is not withheld to obtain consent.

questions.stem: After repair, H. pylori was found. Before discharge, the client describes the plan. For each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll take all the antibiotics for the full 14 days with my omeprazole."
"I'll switch from ibuprofen to acetaminophen for my back."
"The bismuth may turn my stools black."
"I'll keep smoking because it helps my stress."
"I'll be retested after treatment to make sure the infection is gone."
"I can stop omeprazole once the pain goes."

rationale.correct: Teaching covers completing eradication therapy, avoiding NSAIDs and smoking, expected bismuth effects and retesting.

perOption.r4:c1: Smoking delays ulcer healing; offer cessation help.

questions.stem: Which safety actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the head of the bed up and check the swallow before oral lactulose
Low bed, bed alarm and frequent rounding
Keep a bedside commode close and help with toileting
Protect the skin around the anus
Apply wrist restraints to stop the client getting up

questions.stem: A nasogastric (NG) tube is ordered to low intermittent suction. For each part of NG care, select the safe actions.

options.text: Mark the tube at the nostril and check the mark each shift
Confirm placement by injecting air and listening
Keep the blue vent (pigtail) open and above the stomach
Measure and record drainage every shift
Clamp the vent to stop it leaking
Give mouth and nostril care regularly
Tape the tube tightly against the nostril edge

rationale.correct: Safe NG care: x-ray placement, mark checks, an open vent, measured drainage and skin care.

perOption.d: Prevents suction damage to the stomach lining.
perOption.f: Causes the tube to stick to the stomach wall.

questions.stem: For each statement, indicate whether it is accurate or inaccurate.

rows.text: Alcohol hand rub kills C. difficile spores
Spores survive on surfaces for months
The client needs a private room with its own toilet

questions.stem: The nurse audits infection control on the unit. For each observation, indicate whether it meets the standard or needs correction.

rows.text: Staff wash hands with soap and water after leaving the room
The room is cleaned daily with a bleach-based product
A visitor wears a gown and gloves in the room

questions.educationalObjective: Evaluate C. difficile infection control on a unit.

exhibits.title: Unit audit, day 4
exhibits.body: The client went to surgery on day 3 for colectomy.

exhibits.title: Emergency department, 1500
exhibits.body: A 58-year-old client has had burning upper abdominal pain for months that eased after meals. The client smokes and takes ibuprofen 800 mg three times daily for back pain. An hour ago the client had sudden, severe pain across the upper abdomen spreading to the right shoulder. The client lies very still with the knees drawn up. The abdomen is rigid and board-like, with rebound tenderness; bowel sounds are absent.

exhibits.title: Medical unit, 0800
exhibits.body: A 61-year-old client with alcohol-related cirrhosis is confused and sleepy this morning, after being alert yesterday. The client has had no bowel movement for 3 days and was given lorazepam 1 mg last night for sleep. When the arms are held out with wrists extended, the hands flap. Breath has a sweet, musty odor.

exhibits.title: Surgical unit, admission 0600
exhibits.body: A 70-year-old client who had a hysterectomy and an appendectomy years ago has had cramping abdominal pain that comes in waves for 18 hours, with repeated vomiting. The abdomen is distended. High-pitched, tinkling bowel sounds are heard. No stool or flatus since yesterday. CT: small bowel obstruction from adhesions.

caseStudies.title: Severe C. difficile colitis and toxic megacolon

exhibits.title: Medical unit, day 1
exhibits.body: A 72-year-old client was treated with clindamycin 2 weeks ago for a skin infection and takes omeprazole daily. The client now has 12 watery, foul-smelling stools a day, cramping and a distended abdomen. The client shares a bathroom with another client.
